title: Assessment of natural Immunoglobulin M/AIM Deficiency in Thoracic Transplantation
summary:
In this observational study, we want to find out how often people have a deficiency of a certain antibody in their blood after a heart or lung transplant. To do this, we measure the level of this antibody once before the transplant and several times afterwards during the hospital stay. In this way, we want to see whether the operation or the drugs that suppress the immune system change this level. Since we are only observing, we do not administer any additional medication, even if a deficiency is found.

Our second objective is to examine whether such a deficiency after the operation is associated with more complications or a higher risk of severe progression.

The study builds on an earlier investigation conducted by our clinic. At that time, however, only people with planned heart surgery without transplantation and without medication to suppress the immune system were examined. Now we want to focus specifically on people who have undergone heart and lung transplants.

The results should help us decide whether a further study is needed in which additional medication is specifically administered to see whether it helps patients. Our current study is therefore a kind of preliminary study to enable us to plan such a later investigation properly.
conditions: Other interstitial pulmonary diseases with fibrosis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with terminal heart and/or lung failure who are receiving an isolated heart transplant or an isolated lung transplant
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Written informed consent from the patient
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Lack of consent
- Combined procedure (multiple organ transplant)
- Re-transplantation
